Emma — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from the discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the validation run.

Key takeaways (what we heard):
- Primary application: real-time triage assistant embedded in Orion's clinician UI (streaming single-turn completions).
- Latency target: P95 <= 300 ms from first byte (streaming) for prompts up to 400 tokens.
- Concurrency: 35–45 concurrent active sessions during clinic peak; plan for 60 concurrent headroom for bursts.
- Average request profile: user prompt ~120 tokens, expected completion ~220–300 tokens.
- Traffic shape: steady daytime baseline with 3x short spikes lasting 5–10 minutes.
- Data residency / security: US region; standard SOC2 evidence requested (we'll share).

Questions we had for you to confirm before we size reserved capacity:
1) Do you want us to optimize for latency (lower P95) or for cost/throughput (sustained tokens/sec)?
2) Any hard cap on cold-start latency or maximum allowed CPU/GPU selection (e.g., you prefer H100 only)?
3) Expected peak sustained tokens/sec across the cluster (you mentioned ~50k tokens/min on the call — can you confirm units/time window)?

Recommended validation plan (proposal):
- Test matrix: run three baseline configurations across your representative prompt set:
  * H100 (dense FP16), 70B chat variant — target sustained throughput + best tail latency
  * A100-80GB (FP16 + int8 option), 70B chat variant — cost/throughput tradeoff
  * L4 (quantized) with a smaller model variant for lowest-cost, low-latency use cases
- Reserved throughput config: set initial reserved tokens/sec to cover 95% of expected baseline (we propose 8k–10k tps sustained; allow burst to 18k tps with autoscale/burst policy).
- Streaming validation: measure P50/P95/P99 for first-byte and full-response, plus per-request token throughput.
- Concurrency validation: run true-concurrency tests at 40, 60, and 100 sessions to confirm degradation characteristics.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-slo-template.xlsx (populated with the numbers above); gpu-fit-matrix-proposal.pdf (high-level perf/cost tradeoffs).

Hi Emma / Mina — jumping in with a pragmatic proposal for the validation matrix and what we should measure to make the right dedicated recommendation.

Short summary: H100 gives the best raw throughput for large model variants and typically wins on P95 for streaming across long responses when the kernels are tuned. A100-80GB is more cost-efficient and, with int8 quantization on compatible models, often meets P95 for smaller sequence lengths — but you might need an extra node to hit the same sustained tokens/sec. L4 (or smaller T4-like cards) can be used for a scaled-down model variant for baseline low-latency requests.

Concrete plan:
1) Validation runs (we will instrument for token-level latency):
   - Run your prompt set against the 70B chat variant on H100 at three reserved throughput points: 8k, 12k, 18k tokens/sec sustained (10-minute windows).
   - Repeat on A100-80GB with same reserved points (note: expected CPU overhead differences — we'll measure host-level syscalls).
   - Run a smaller 13B-quantized profile on L4 to validate sub-200ms P95 for short completions.
2) Failure modes to capture: queueing latency at the ingress, KV cache miss penalties, and streaming jitter when concurrent sessions spike.
3) Success criteria to accept a configuration as "right-fit":
   - P95(first byte) <= 300ms across the 10-minute sustained windows at the reserved throughput point.
   - No more than 5% request error rate and <2% tail amplification beyond P99 threshold.
   - Cost estimate within the committed capacity budget we agree with Sales Ops.

Operational notes: Redwood Dedicated supports a reserved throughput setting per-customer plus a configurable burst buffer. For Orion I suggest we start with reserved=12k tps, burst headroom to 24k tps, and auto-fallback to the smaller model variant if sustained load exceeds the buffer. This gives a good balance between cost predictability and reliability.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the test (bench commands, perf dashboards, and a minimal checklist) and post it to the HubSpot deal link. If you want, we can also run one quick dry-run on our side using a synthetically similar prompt set to validate the harness before the joint window.
